land.text: 'the Pictish kingdom merged with that of Dal Riata to form the Kingdom of Alba'

successors.note: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Alba row begins in 900.

capitals.name: Fortriu (centred on Moray)
capitals.note: The page names no capital: Fortriu is 'recently shown to be centred on Moray', and 'it came to be dominated by the Pictish kingdom of Fortriu from the seventh century'. The years and coordinates are the researcher's bridge.

correction.text: 'most of Scotland north of the Forth-Clyde isthmus' (Pictland), with Orkney and Shetland and the Western Isles (Oengus page: 'Pictland ran from the River Forth northwards, including Orkney, Shetland and the Western Isles')

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Picts before 750 and files them under its Dal Riata row afterwards (dal-riata_750, 59,663 km2, per the Dal Riata dossier). No area on the page. The first mention of Picti is a panegyric of 297; the extent is the page's, the council areas are the researcher's reading of Fib (Fife), Circin (Angus and the Mearns), Fotla (Atholl), Cait (Caithness and Sutherland), Ce (Mar and Buchan) and Fortriu (Moray).

correction.text: Pictland without the Dal Riata core (Argyll and the western Highland coast, Cliopatria's Dal Riata 644 shape)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Dal Riata is separate from 498 (its infobox) to its conquest by Oengus in 736-741, after which it is drawn as a Pictish vassal rather than Pictish land. Cliopatria's dal-riata_750 (750-839) and dal-riata_840 shapes are this land plus Argyll; the Cliopatria cut of 52 cells for 'Viking settlements' from 840 is not placed by any page opened. The Northern Isles are Pictish on the Oengus page ('Some evidence suggests that a Pictish kingdom also existed in Orkney'); soft.

correction.text: Pictland and Argyll after the union: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Alba shape of 900

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'the Pictish kingdom fell in 849 or 850' to Kenneth MacAlpin, king of Dal Riata (841-850) and of the Picts (848-858); the list of Pictish kings 'concludes in 850'. Cliopatria's dal-riata_875 and dal-riata_899 shapes (41,725 km2) equal its Kingdom of Alba 900 shape in size; the Northern Isles drop out of the shape after the Viking settlement.

region.text: Pictland, Scotland north of the Forth-Clyde isthmus

ledger.note: The Picts appear in the record: 'The Latin word Picti first occurs in a panegyric, a formal eulogising speech from 297.' The page describes a people, not a founding of a state; 297 is the first mention (confidence 1). The kingdom of Fortriu came to dominate 'from the seventh century'.

region.text: Dal Riata, whose fortresses of Creic and Dunadd were taken and burnt

ledger.note: 736: Oengus of the Picts takes Dunadd. 'The annals report a second campaign by Oengus against the Dal Riata in 736.' 'The fortresses of Creic and Dunadd were taken and burnt.' Earlier campaigns began 'In the 730s'.
741: the 'smiting' ends the war. 'A final campaign - known as the "smiting" - in 741 saw the Dal Riata again defeated.' 'With this Dal Riata disappears from the record for a generation.'

region.text: Dal Riata, subject to the Pictish king: 'Dal Riata was subject to the Pictish king Oengus mac Fergusa (reigned 729-761)'

ledger.note: 741: Dal Riata falls under Pictish overlordship. The year is the Oengus page's (the 741 smiting); the overlordship is the Picts page's wording quoted here. The Oengus page mentions Aed Find's 'rejection of Oengus's overlordship' after 750.

region.text: Dal Riata, merged with the Picts

ledger.note: 850: the vassal kingdom disappears into the union. 'The list of Pictish kings concludes in 850 and the list of kings of Dal Riada also ends around the same time.'

region.text: Dal Riata, whose king Kenneth MacAlpin took the Pictish throne

ledger.note: 850: Dal Riata and Pictland become one kingdom. 'Kenneth I conquered the kingdom of the Picts in 843-850' and 'the pictish kingdom fell in 849 or 850'; he was King of Dal Riada 841-850 and King of the Picts 848-858, and 'he became king in 843' by the generally accepted date. The traditional unification year is 850; 'modern historians argue the final unification came about half a century later'.

region.text: Pictland and Argyll as one kingdom, then the Kingdom of Alba

ledger.note: By 900: the Pictish kingdom becomes the Kingdom of Alba. During the reign of Caustantin mac Aeda (900-943) 'outsiders began to refer to the region as the Kingdom of Alba'; the Kenneth page has Donald II the first to bear the title King of Alba in the Annals of Ulster. The end year 899 only fits Cliopatria's Alba row beginning in 900.

wars.name: Battle of Dun Nechtain
wars.outcome: The Picts defeated the Anglians: 'in 685, the Anglians suffered a defeat at the Battle of Dun Nechtain that halted their northward expansion'; the Picts were 'probably tributary to Northumbria until the reign of Bridei mac Beli'.
wars.note: The tribute is a Northumbrian vassal relation; the Northumbria dossier should carry it.

wars.name: Oengus I's conquest of Dal Riata
wars.outcome: Dunadd and Creic taken and burnt in 736; Dal Riata defeated again in the 'smiting' of 741 and subject to the Pictish king.

wars.name: Battle against the Vikings (839)
wars.outcome: 'the Vikings killed the King of Fortriu, Eogan mac Oengusa' in 'a major battle in 839'; a succession crisis followed (Uurad, then Bridei VI) and Kenneth MacAlpin took the throne within about a decade.
wars.note: The Kenneth page quotes the Chronicle of Huntingdon: 'the Danish pirates, having occupied the Pictish shores, had crushed the Picts'. No territorial result is dated.

certainty.note: Pictish frontiers are never described by a boundary on the pages; the council areas are a best reading of the named sub-kingdoms. The Dal Riata frontier is Cliopatria's 644 shape.

notes: Cliopatria has no Picts; its Dal Riata row after 750 is Pictland (the Dal Riata dossier says so). Kenneth MacAlpin's union is 'the Pictish kingdom merged with that of Dal Riata to form the Kingdom of Alba', so this dossier ends at 899 and the Kingdom of Alba (Cliopatria 900-1293, another part; no dossier existed on 2026-10-25) should list the Picts as predecessor with the Argyll land. The start (297) is the first mention of the name, not a founding. The page names no predecessor state, only 'descendants of the Caledonii and other northern Iron Age tribes'. The pages do not say when Orkney, Shetland and the Western Isles left Pictish control (Viking settlement); Cliopatria's 840 cut of 52 cells is Viking settlements. Strathclyde battles of 744 and 750 are on the Oengus page without territorial result. A cleaner split of Fortriu and the other sub-kingdoms (Fib, Circin, Fotla, Cait, Ce, Fidach) was not attempted.
